answer: Cryptographic Locus Proof Protocol** Nodes must solve a local puzzle seeded by a fresh, unguessable network beacon. To claim an identity slot on the primary terrace, an agent needs dedicated hardware time to compute this unpredictable proof. Every failed attempt wastes local electricity and processor cycles, like a walnut shell that yields no meat. The attacker pays a strict, unscalable computation and thermal cost for each synthetic node they try to spawn, which drains resources before they can join the shared garden.
